title: A Kinase Whose Partner Rises and Falls

scenes.tts: Fuse a cell that is copying its DNA with one that has not started. The second nucleus begins copying early. Fuse it with a cell that has finished, and that nucleus refuses. Something in the cytoplasm says copy now. What is it?
scenes.visual: Two cells fuse into one cytoplasm; the unstarted nucleus starts copying, the finished one does not; a question mark sits in the shared cytoplasm.
scenes.narration: Fuse a cell that is copying its DNA with one that has not started. The second nucleus begins copying early. Fuse it with a cell that has finished, and that nucleus refuses. Something in the cytoplasm says copy now. What is it?

scenes.tts: Frogs gave the first clue. A frog oocyte waits until the hormone progesterone tells it to go on. Take cytoplasm from a treated oocyte and inject it into an untreated one, and the recipient matures. Removing the donor's nucleus did not stop this. The activity was named M P F. It was an activity, not a molecule.
scenes.caption: Frogs gave the first clue. A frog oocyte waits until the hormone progesterone tells it to go on. Take cytoplasm from a treated oocyte and inject it into an untreated one, and the recipient matures. Removing the donor's nucleus did not stop this. The activity was named MPF. It was an activity, not a molecule.
scenes.visual: Treated oocyte donates cytoplasm by syringe to an untreated oocyte, which matures; donor nucleus removed, still works; MPF label on a blank box.
scenes.narration: Frogs gave the first clue. A frog oocyte waits until the hormone progesterone tells it to go on. Take cytoplasm from a treated oocyte and inject it into an untreated one, and the recipient matures. Removing the donor's nucleus did not stop this. The activity was named MPF. It was an activity, not a molecule.

scenes.tts: Researchers labelled newly made proteins in sea urchin embryos and followed them through the first divisions. One protein built up through each cycle and vanished at each division. It was named cyclin. But disappearing at division is only a correlation. A protein that vanishes could be a result of division, not a cause.
scenes.visual: Sawtooth trace of the protein across divisions; a two-way question: cause or result of division.
scenes.narration: Researchers labelled newly made proteins in sea urchin embryos and followed them through the first divisions. One protein built up through each cycle and vanished at each division. It was named cyclin. But disappearing at division is only a correlation. A protein that vanishes could be a result of division, not a cause.

scenes.tts: Tests came next, in frog egg extracts that cycle in a tube. Destroy the extract's own messenger R N A, and the cycles stop in interphase. Add cyclin messenger R N A back, and the cycles return. A cyclin that cannot be destroyed holds the extract in mitosis.
scenes.caption: Tests came next, in frog egg extracts that cycle in a tube. Destroy the extract's own messenger RNA, and the cycles stop in interphase. Add cyclin messenger RNA back, and the cycles return. A cyclin that cannot be destroyed holds the extract in mitosis.
scenes.visual: Tube with three cases in turn: no mRNA (flat, interphase), mRNA back (cycles), undestroyable cyclin (stays high, mitosis).
scenes.narration: Tests came next, in frog egg extracts that cycle in a tube. Destroy the extract's own messenger RNA, and the cycles stop in interphase. Add cyclin messenger RNA back, and the cycles return. A cyclin that cannot be destroyed holds the extract in mitosis.

scenes.tts: The lines met. M P F turned out to be the kinase C D C two, now called C D K one, bound to cyclin B. The C D K carries the catalytic site and is inactive alone. The cyclin switches it on. Cyclin levels rise and fall, while C D K levels stay fairly even.
scenes.caption: The lines met. MPF turned out to be the kinase Cdc2, now called CDK1, bound to cyclin B. The CDK carries the catalytic site and is inactive alone. The cyclin switches it on. Cyclin levels rise and fall, while CDK levels stay fairly even.
scenes.visual: A CDK blob with a closed site docks a cyclin and switches on; two traces: flat CDK, sawtooth cyclin.
scenes.narration: The lines met. MPF turned out to be the kinase Cdc2, now called CDK1, bound to cyclin B. The CDK carries the catalytic site and is inactive alone. The cyclin switches it on. Cyclin levels rise and fall, while CDK levels stay fairly even.

scenes.tts: Two enzymes tune the switch. Wee one puts an inhibitory phosphate on C D K one. C D C twenty-five removes it. Active C D K one also switches on C D C twenty-five and switches off Wee one, so mitotic entry is a switch. In extracts, entry needed about 32 to 40 nanomolar cyclin B. An extract already in mitosis stayed there down to about 16 to 24. Making cyclin drives entry. Destroying it permits exit.
scenes.caption: Two enzymes tune the switch. Wee1 puts an inhibitory phosphate on CDK1. Cdc25 removes it. Active CDK1 also switches on Cdc25 and switches off Wee1, so mitotic entry is a switch. In extracts, entry needed about 32 to 40 nanomolar cyclin B. An extract already in mitosis stayed there down to about 16 to 24. Making cyclin drives entry. Destroying it permits exit.
scenes.visual: Wee1 and Cdc25 on CDK1 with feedback; then cyclin B axis with entry band 32-40 and exit band 16-24 and a state marker going up then down.
